source.note: the sample the operator supplied (37.5 s, MPEG-1 layer III, 256 kbit/s, 44.1 kHz stereo); not recorded by the prototype, which has no microphone

pcm.what: the source decoded to 16-bit mono PCM and sealed (PCM frames of 20 ms, 8 a block); 'cipher' is the ciphertext at the place of every sample

wrong_key.what: the keystream of a block key that differs in ONE bit, applied without the tag check (the implementation refuses the block: its commitment and its tag fail)

differences.what: the same audio sealed twice (a new clip key each time, as the system does)
the audio with ONE sample changed by one step, sealed again (a new clip key)
one sample changed, SAME key and nonce (the system never does this): only that byte differs

compressed.what: the source file itself (compressed audio is already close to random; the sealed blocks are indistinguishable from random)

shape.what: the same audio encoded at a variable bit rate (libmp3lame -q:a 5): the size of every frame follows the sound. Per-frame encryption (SRTP, or AES-GCM per frame) keeps those sizes; the sealed blocks all have one size
